rendering.persona_description: Zanele is a 24-year-old woman who works as a junior paralegal at a small firm, a job she chose because she likes the idea of things being precise and on the record. She lives with her older sister in a two-bedroom apartment and spends most weekends visiting her parents nearby. She enjoys baking elaborate cakes for friends' birthdays, though she's been too busy with work lately to do it as often.
rendering.clinical_context: Zanele has no mental-health presentation. Like most people, she occasionally has a passing thought that she left the stove on, forgot to lock the door, or made a small error in a document, but these thoughts come and go without lasting distress and without her doing anything to neutralize them. She has never sought or needed mental-health treatment.
rendering.behavioral_description: She occasionally mentions double-checking whether she locked the door or turned off the stove before leaving, in the same brief, matter-of-fact way most people mention checking their phone before heading out. She agrees readily when a plan is suggested to her, saying things like 'that makes sense' or 'okay, I'll try that,' and generally follows through without difficulty. She rarely pushes back or argues; instead she tends to go along with suggestions and moves the conversation along easily.
